fullPassage:
Keep Trying and Keep Hoping

People all over the world are making efforts to save the environment. Some have succeeded, some have failed, but remember that every little change helps.

Seaweed Hamburger Packages

Most food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. Believe it or not, your hamburger could soon be wrapped in seaweed. A team of researchers has invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia. The new coating material works almost like plastic, helping prevent food from sticking to paper, while also breaking down more easily than plastic. The material can be made into thin films that can be coated on various surfaces, such as paper or fabric. The fast-food industry is welcoming the news, with major restaurant brands planning to choose greener packaging by 2025.

Your Leather Bags Are Going Un-Leather

What is made of leather? Bags, shoes, clothes, car seats, and the list goes on. Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find more environmentally friendly options. The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. To many customers' relief, since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested, and some have been proven to make alternative leathers. Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets. As consumer demand for eco-friendly products continues to grow, more will be invented and used. The market for eco-friendly leather alternatives is growing rapidly. In 2022, the market was valued at $725 million and is expected to reach $1.2 billion by 2030.

questions.passage: ①<u>People</u> all over the world are making efforts to save the environment. ②<u>Some</u> have succeeded, some have failed, but remember that every little change <u>help</u>. ③<u>Most</u> food packaging is coated with plastic, <u>making</u> it nearly impossible to recycle. ④<u>Believe</u> it or not, your hamburger could soon be <u>wrapped</u> in seaweed. A team of researchers <u>has</u> invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 모든 작은 변화가 도움이 된다(helps). help → helps. 주어 every little change(단수) → 동사 helps
det.analysis:
✅ ① help → helps: every + 단수명사 → 단수동사 필요
❌ ② making: 분사구문(결과) 정상
❌ ③ wrapped: be wrapped in(수동태) 정상
❌ ④ has: a team(단수) → has invented 정상
det.tip: every + 단수명사 → 단수동사. every student has (O) / every student have (X)

questions.passage: Oil-①<u>based</u> leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So ②<u>companies</u> have been <u>trying</u> to find more environmentally friendly options. The ③<u>first</u> success came in the 1990s, <u>when</u> a company made leather from pineapple leaves. To ④<u>many</u> customers' relief, since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been <u>testing</u>, and some have been proven <u>to make</u> alternative leathers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 많은 친환경 재료가 시험되었다(tested). testing → tested. 수동태(have been tested) 필요
det.analysis:
✅ ③ testing → tested: have been + p.p.(수동태). 재료가 '시험되었다'이므로 수동
❌ ① trying: have been trying(현재완료진행) 정상
❌ ② when: 시간 관계부사(the 1990s 선행) 정상
❌ ④ to make: be proven to V(~하는 것으로 입증되다) 정상
det.tip: have been + V-ing(능동진행) vs have been + p.p.(수동완료). 주어가 행위 대상이면 수동

questions.passage: ①<u>Most</u> food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. A ②<u>team</u> of researchers has invented an alternative ④<u>material</u> from seaweed native to South Australia. The new ③<u>coating</u> material works almost like plastic, <u>helping</u> prevent food from sticking to paper, while also <u>breaking</u> down more easily than plastic. The material can be made into thin films <u>that</u> can be coated on various surfaces. The fast-food industry is welcoming the news, with major restaurant brands <u>plan</u> to choose greener packaging by 2025.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 주요 레스토랑 브랜드들이 더 친환경적인 포장을 선택할 계획인(planning). plan → planning. with + O + V-ing(분사구문)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ plan → planning: with + 명사 + V-ing(부대상황). with brands planning
❌ ① helping: 분사구문(결과) 정상
❌ ② breaking: while also + V-ing 병렬 정상
❌ ③ that: 주격 관계대명사(films를 수식) 정상
det.tip: with + O + V-ing: 부대상황 분사구문. with brands planning = 브랜드들이 계획하면서

questions.passage: ①<u>What</u> is made of leather? ②<u>Bags</u>, shoes, clothes, car seats, and the list goes on. Oil-③<u>based</u> leathers, <u>which</u> make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce. ④<u>Grape</u> waste from the wine industry and a mushroom <u>growing</u> from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 농업 폐기물에서 재배된(grown) 버섯. growing → grown. 버섯이 '재배된' 것이므로 과거분사
det.analysis:
✅ ② growing → grown: a mushroom grown from = ~에서 재배된 버섯. 수동 의미 과거분사
❌ ① which: 계속적 용법 관계대명사(Oil-based leathers 선행) 정상
❌ ③ to grow: continue to V(계속 ~하다) 정상
❌ ④ is expected: 수동태(~될 것으로 예상되다) 정상
det.tip: growing(자라는/능동) vs grown(재배된/수동). 뒤에 from farming waste(~에서)가 오면 수동 의미

questions.passage: ①<u>People</u> all over the world are making efforts to save the environment. ②<u>Most</u> food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. A ③<u>team</u> of researchers has invented an <u>alternative</u> material from seaweed native to South Australia. The new ④<u>coating</u> material works almost like plastic, helping prevent food from <u>sticking</u> to paper, while also breaking down more <u>hardly</u> than plastic. The material can be made into thin films that can be coated on <u>various</u> surfaces, such as paper or fabric.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 플라스틱보다 더 쉽게(easily) 분해된다. hardly(거의 ~않게)는 원문의 easily(쉽게)를 잘못 바꾼 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ hardly(거의 ~않게) → easily(쉽게)가 원문. 플라스틱 대안의 장점은 쉽게 분해되는 것
❌ ① alternative(대안의): 원문 그대로
❌ ② sticking(붙는): 원문 그대로
❌ ④ various(다양한): 원문 그대로
det.tip: easily(쉽게) ↔ hardly(거의 ~않게). easy는 '쉬운', hard는 '어려운'이지만 hardly는 '거의 ~않는'이라는 뜻

questions.passage: Oil-①<u>based</u> leathers, which make up the <u>majority</u> of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to <u>produce</u> and a long time to break down. So ②<u>companies</u> have been trying to find more environmentally friendly options. ③<u>Grape</u> waste from the wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets. As ④<u>consumer</u> demand for eco-friendly products continues to <u>shrink</u>, more will be invented and used. The market for eco-friendly leather alternatives is growing <u>rapidly</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 소비자 수요가 계속 증가(grow)하고 있다. shrink(줄어들다)는 원문의 grow(증가하다)를 잘못 바꾼 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ shrink(줄어들다) → grow(증가하다)가 원문. 뒤에 '더 많이 발명되고 사용될 것'이라는 내용이 근거
❌ ① majority(대다수): 원문 그대로
❌ ② produce(생산하다): 원문 그대로
❌ ④ rapidly(빠르게): 원문 그대로
det.tip: grow(증가하다) ↔ shrink(줄어들다). continues to grow → 계속 증가한다

questions.passage: Most food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. Believe it or not, your hamburger could soon be wrapped in seaweed. A team of researchers has invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"해초 기반 소재는 북미 지역의 해초에서 만들어졌다."

det.korean: 해초 소재는 남호주(South Australia) 토착 해초에서 만들어졌다. 북미가 아님.
det.analysis:
✅ F: 원문은 seaweed native to South Australia(남호주 토착 해초). 북미 지역이 아님
❌ T: 지역이 다름
det.tip: native to South Australia = 남호주 토착. 지역명을 정확히 확인하는 문제

questions.passage: The fast-food industry is welcoming the news, with major restaurant brands planning to choose greener packaging by 2025. Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"패스트푸드 산업은 친환경 포장재 소식을 환영하고 있다."

det.korean: 패스트푸드 산업이 이 소식을 환영(welcoming)하고 있다. 원문과 일치.
det.analysis:
✅ T: The fast-food industry is welcoming the news와 정확히 일치
❌ F: 원문에 명시적으로 welcoming이라고 되어 있음
det.tip: welcoming the news = 소식을 환영하다. 패러프레이징: 친환경 포장재 소식 = the news(해초 소재 뉴스)

questions.passage: The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. To many customers' relief, since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested, and some have been proven to make alternative leathers. Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"최초의 친환경 가죽 성공 사례는 2000년대에 나왔다."

det.korean: 최초의 성공은 1990년대(the 1990s)에 나왔다. 2000년대가 아님.
det.analysis:
✅ F: 원문은 The first success came in the 1990s. 2000년대가 아니라 1990년대
❌ T: 연대가 다름
det.tip: the 1990s = 1990년대. 숫자/연대를 살짝 바꾸는 함정에 주의

questions.passage: Most food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. Believe it or not, your hamburger could soon be wrapped in seaweed. A team of researchers has invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia. The new coating material works almost like plastic, helping prevent food from sticking to paper, while also __________. The material can be made into thin films that can be coated on various surfaces.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: lasting longer than any other material
breaking down more easily than plastic

det.korean: 새 코팅 소재는 플라스틱보다 더 쉽게 분해된다(breaking down more easily than plastic).
det.analysis:
✅ ④ breaking down more easily than plastic: 원문 일치. while also 뒤에 분사구문으로 연결
❌ ① lasting longer: 오래 지속되는 것은 언급 없음
❌ ② costing less: 비용 비교는 원문에 없음
❌ ③ absorbing moisture: 수분 흡수는 원문에 없음
det.tip: while also + V-ing: helping과 병렬 분사구문. 플라스틱 대체재의 장점 = 쉽게 분해

questions.passage: Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find more environmentally friendly options. The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets. As consumer demand for eco-friendly products continues to grow, __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: fewer companies will invest in leather alternatives
the price of oil-based leather will decrease
more will be invented and used
traditional leather production will remain unchanged

det.korean: 소비자 수요가 계속 증가하면서, 더 많은 것이 발명되고 사용될 것이다(more will be invented and used).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ more will be invented and used: 원문 일치. 수요 증가 → 더 많은 발명·사용
❌ ① fewer companies: 수요 증가와 모순
❌ ② price decrease: 가격 하락은 원문에 없음
❌ ④ remain unchanged: 변화 없음은 성장 맥락과 모순
det.tip: as ~ continues to grow, more will be ~ : 증가하는 수요에 따른 결과 추론

questions.passage: Most food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. A team of researchers has invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia. The new coating material works almost like plastic, helping prevent food from sticking to paper. The material can be made into thin films that can be coated on various surfaces, such as paper or fabric. The fast-food industry is welcoming the news, with major restaurant brands planning to choose greener packaging by 2025.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 새로운 코팅 소재는 다양한 표면에 적용할 수 있다.
해초 소재는 플라스틱보다 음식이 더 잘 붙는다.
패스트푸드 산업은 해초 포장재를 거부하고 있다.
새로운 소재는 종이에만 코팅할 수 있다.

det.korean: 소재는 종이나 천 등 다양한 표면에 코팅 가능.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 다양한 표면에 적용 가능: coated on various surfaces, such as paper or fabric
❌ ② 음식이 더 잘 붙는다: 반대. helping prevent food from sticking
❌ ③ 거부하고 있다: 반대. welcoming the news
❌ ④ 종이에만: various surfaces이므로 종이만이 아님
det.tip: various surfaces = 다양한 표면. such as paper or fabric = 예를 들어 종이나 천

questions.passage: Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets. The market for eco-friendly leather alternatives is growing rapidly. In 2022, the market was valued at $725 million and is expected to reach $1.2 billion by 2030.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 석유 기반 가죽은 분해에 오랜 시간이 걸린다.
최초의 친환경 가죽은 포도 찌꺼기로 만들어졌다.
버섯이 가죽 같은 시트로 전환되는 데 성공했다.

det.korean: 최초 성공은 파인애플 잎(pineapple leaves)으로 만든 것이다. 포도 찌꺼기가 아님.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 불일치: 최초 성공은 pineapple leaves(파인애플 잎). Grape waste는 이후 사례
❌ ① 일치: a long time to break down
❌ ③ 일치: valued at $725 million
❌ ④ 일치: a mushroom ~ turned into leather-like sheets
det.tip: first success = pineapple leaves(1990s). grape waste와 mushroom은 이후 사례

questions.passage: ①<u>People</u> all over the world are making efforts to save the environment. ②<u>Most</u> food packaging is <u>④<u>coating</u></u> with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. A ③<u>team</u> of researchers has invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia. The new coating material works almost like plastic, helping <u>prevent</u> food from sticking to paper. The material can be made into thin films that can be <u>coated</u> on various surfaces. The fast-food industry is <u>welcoming</u> the news.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 식품 포장은 플라스틱으로 코팅되어 있다(coated). coating → coated. 수동태(is coated) 필요
det.analysis:
✅ ① coating → coated: is + p.p.(수동태). 포장이 '코팅되는' 것이므로 수동
❌ ② prevent: help + 동사원형(사역동사) 정상
❌ ③ coated: can be coated(수동태) 정상
❌ ④ welcoming: is welcoming(현재진행) 정상
det.tip: is coated with = ~으로 코팅되어 있다(수동). is coating = 코팅하고 있다(능동). 주어가 packaging이므로 수동

questions.passage: Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find more environmentally friendly options. The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. To many customers' relief, since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested, and some have been proven to make alternative leathers. Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets. As consumer demand for eco-friendly products continues to grow, more will be invented and used. The market for eco-friendly leather alternatives is growing rapidly. In 2022, the market was valued at $725 million and is expected to reach $1.2 billion by 2030.
questions.stem: 본문에서 찾아 다음 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오. "기업들은 석유 기반 가죽의 대안으로 더 환경 친화적인 선택지를 찾으려고 __________ 해왔다." (조건: 1단어 사용) (1단어)

det.korean: 기업들은 더 환경 친화적인 선택지를 찾으려고 노력(trying)해왔다.
det.analysis: ✅ trying: have been trying to find(~하려고 노력해왔다)에서 trying
det.tip: try to V = ~하려고 노력하다. have been trying = 계속 노력해왔다(현재완료진행)

questions.passage: To many customers' relief, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested. Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming waste have been __________ (success) turned into leather-like sheets.
questions.stem: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (조건: 1단어 사용) (1단어)

det.korean: 포도 찌꺼기와 버섯이 성공적으로(successfully) 가죽 시트로 전환되었다.
det.analysis: ✅ successfully: turned(동사)를 수식하므로 부사형 필요. success(명사) → successfully(부사)
det.tip: success(명사) → successful(형용사) → successfully(부사). 동사를 수식할 때는 부사

questions.passage: Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find more environmentally friendly options. The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. To many customers' relief, since then, __________.
questions.stem:

questions.passage: Most food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. Believe it or not, your hamburger could soon be wrapped in seaweed. A team of researchers has invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia. The new coating material works almost like plastic, helping prevent food from sticking to paper, while also breaking down more easily than plastic. The material can be made into thin films that can be coated on various surfaces, such as paper or fabric. The fast-food industry is welcoming the news, with major restaurant brands planning to choose greener packaging by 2025.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 글은 해초에서 만든 친환경 포장재 개발에 대한 내용이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 해초 기반 친환경 포장재의 개발: 해초에서 플라스틱 대안 소재를 발명한 이야기
❌ ① 재활용 방법: 재활용이 어렵다는 배경일 뿐
❌ ② 마케팅 전략: 패스트푸드 산업은 부분적 언급
❌ ④ 생태학적 특성: 해초의 생태 설명이 아님
det.tip: 글의 핵심 = alternative material from seaweed. 배경(플라스틱 문제)과 주제(해초 대안)를 구분

questions.passage: What is made of leather? Bags, shoes, clothes, car seats, and the list goes on. Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find more environmentally friendly options. The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets. As consumer demand for eco-friendly products continues to grow, more will be invented and used. The market for eco-friendly leather alternatives is growing rapidly. In 2022, the market was valued at $725 million and is expected to reach $1.2 billion by 2030.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 요약문으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 석유 기반 가죽은 환경에 해롭지만, 대안을 찾기는 불가능하다.
파인애플 잎이 가죽의 유일한 친환경 대안이다.
친환경 가죽 시장은 정부 규제 덕분에 성장하고 있다.
기업들이 다양한 친환경 소재로 가죽 대안을 개발하며, 시장이 빠르게 성장하고 있다.

det.korean: 석유 기반 가죽의 환경 문제 → 친환경 대안 개발(파인애플, 포도, 버섯) → 시장 급성장
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 다양한 친환경 소재 + 시장 급성장: 글 전체 흐름을 정확히 요약
❌ ① 대안 불가능: 여러 대안이 이미 성공
❌ ② 유일한 대안: 파인애플 외에도 포도, 버섯 등
❌ ③ 정부 규제: 원문에 정부 규제 언급 없음. 소비자 수요가 동력
det.tip: 요약문은 글 전체(문제→시도→결과)를 포괄해야 함. 부분적 사실만 언급하는 선지는 오답
